correctness.rationale: A rectangular kernel-count calculation gives the universal lower bound under arbitrary input-independent rank-at-most-r masks and secret invertible transforms. Uniform exact-rank masking has Fourier coefficients equal to normalized bilinear-forms eigenvalues; published spectral monotonicity makes rank one maximal for q>=3 and for binary nonsquare rectangles, and its coefficient equals the lower bound. Exact-integer checks reproduce the identities and the excluded binary-square exception.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The September 2026 masking preprint gives the same square converse expression but only factor-two achievability with its proposed masks. The bilinear-forms spectral theorems are older and are not claimed as new. Exact and synonymous searches found no prior connection yielding the exact-rank-shell minimax theorem or its rectangular extension. The recency of the motivating preprint leaves a material simultaneous-work risk.

value.rationale: The theorem closes the new nonbinary low-rank masking achievability/converse gap exactly at every finite parameter, remains optimal against secret invertible transformations, extends to rectangular matrices, and uses a mask distribution that can be sampled with standard full-rank factors.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, or a guarantee of first discovery.
